title: Lifecycle-lite SDK sprint kit and cheatnotebook
content:
Purpose: compact, practical sprint kit for a 3-day developer experience effort to ship a minimal, instrumented SDK quickstart. This is intentionally opinionated: small surface area, repeatable checks, observability-first.

Audience: SDK engineers, DE advocates, solutions engs running quickstarts with customers.

High-level goals (3-day sprint):
- Day 0 (prep): create starter repo, minimal README, demo app that calls Redwood API (chat + embeddings)
- Day 1 (core): polish API ergonomics (init, client, streaming), add simple local-mode runner, wire telemetry hooks
- Day 2 (finish): smoke CI, sample prompt set + eval script, docs quickstart and 15-minute demo script

Non-goals:
- Full-blown multi-language parity (pick 1 polyglot language for the sprint)
- Production-grade packaging or enterprise signing

Quick checklist (must-haves for demo success):
- [ ] repo scaffold with: README, LICENSE, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, CONTRIBUTING.md (mini)
- [ ] quickstart README: 3 steps to first response and one embed vector store example
- [ ] example app: serverless/CLI + tiny web UI (one page)
- [ ] CI smoke test that runs 1 request to the hosted api (uses CI token)
- [ ] telemetry: basic timing and token count exported as JSON to stdout (local dev)
- [ ] error handling: transparent retry/backoff policy example (2000ms initial, 2 retries)
- [ ] minimal tests: request shape + response sanity check + prompt regression check

Ergonomic surface (proposal):
- SDK entrypoint: import { Redwood } from '@redwood/sdk-lite'
- new Redwood({ apiKey, mode: 'local' | 'hosted', telemetry: TelemetryClient })
- Methods: client.chat(messages[], opts), client.embed(text[], opts), client.streamChat(...)
- Default sensible timeouts and retries; explicit overrides in opts

Telemetry contract (why tiny matters):
- Events emitted synchronously for local dev; pluggable sink for prod (console | file | OTLP)
- Minimal event set: request_start, request_end, token_count, latency_ms, error
- Schema (flat): { event: string, request_id: uuid, model: string, tokens: int, millis: int, status: "ok" | "err" }
- Implementation note: keep no PII in telemetry; only hash prompt ids if needed

Local-mode runner: fast path to emulate response during no-network (helps demos)
- Provide a small set of canned responses & simple deterministic embed tokenization that mirrors Redwood's real output shape
- CLI switch: --local-seed=foo to vary canned outputs for demos

Prompt set + eval: small binary check for regressions
- tiny_prompts.json: 8 prompts covering greeting, instruction-following, hallucination test, and reranking seed
- eval script: run prompts against staging model (or local runner) and assert key tokens/phrases exist/absent
- Output: pass/fail with per-prompt diff and token counts

Developer flow (15-min demo script):
1) git clone && npm i
2) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=xxx
3) npm run demo:start -> open http://localhost:3000 -> paste prompt -> see streaming tokens
4) run npm run eval to validate sample prompts
5) switch to --local to show deterministic no-network behavior

CLI snippets (quick):
- curl example: curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}'
- node quickstart: const r = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); await r.chat([{role:'user', content:'Summarize this.'}])

Minimal security checklist for quickstarts:
- Do not hardcode API keys in repo. Use env vars and .env.example
- README prominently warns about usage quotas and costs
- Provide guidance for rotating keys and using short-lived demo tokens (if supported)

Gating CI checks (lightweight):
- ci/smoke.sh: runs a single request and validates status 200 and token_count > 0
- ci/prompt-regression.sh: runs tiny_prompts.json against local runner in PRs (fast)
- Gate: require smoke.sh to pass before merging to main

Common friction & mitigation notes (field notes):
- New users confuse 'stream' semantics: add a short paragraph 'streaming is incremental token flow, not guaranteed order' + sample code
- Telemetry overload: keep default sink local and off in CI; allow opt-in OTLP via env var
- Network flakiness in demos: provide local-mode + recorded trace to replay in case of outage

Open questions / TODOs:
- Which language to target first? (JS/TS preferred) -- decision: JS with TypeScript types
- Can we provide ephemeral demo tokens programmatically? who owns back-end? (talk to Solutions Eng ops)
- How to surface cost estimates in quickstart before user runs heavy prompts? insert static examples + token calculator helper

Rollout plan for this sprint kit (next 2 weeks):
- Week 1: implement repo scaffold + core API + local runner + README
- Week 2: add telemetry sinks, CI, prompt eval, and 15-min demo script; run internal playtest with 3 SEs
- Publish: mark repo as experimental, link from playbooks and demo decks

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep API surface to <10 functions; avoid adding complex batching until later
- Make sample app single-file where possible for comprehension
- Add a short video (2-3 mins) recorded by Marcus that walks the 15-min flow

Links / references used while drafting:
- GH scaffold template: GH: redwood-inference/sdk-starter#72
- Internal ticket: JIRA: DEVEXP-158 (telemetry hooks)
- Platform docs reference: CONFLUENCE-PLAT-4201

Nearby follow-up docs to author after MVP:
- packaging and release checklist for SDKs (npm, pypi, jars)
- integration test matrix (models X regions X auth modes)

If you're running the sprint: ping @sofia (Sofia Nguyen) on #devexp and add quick notes to the PR title: "mini-sprint: quickstart + telemetry".

End of notebook.
